tool_input.description: Check non-lenient Calendar.set behavior for invalid day

result:
I wrote `DateUtilsAgentTest` (`src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java`), covering `isSameDay`, `isSameInstant`, `isSameLocalTime`, `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly`, all `add*`/`set*` methods, `toCalendar`, `round`/`truncate`/`ceiling` (Date/Calendar/Object overloads), the day `iterator`, all `getFragmentIn*` variants, `truncatedEquals`/`truncatedCompareTo`, and the public constants — including null checks, type-mismatch `ClassCastException`s, out-of-range `IllegalArgumentException`s, and boundary cases.

79 tests ran, 78 pass, 1 fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testCeilingDateAlreadyOnBoundaryIsUnchanged`** — `DateUtils.ceiling(date, field)` is documented (and behaves, by comparison with `round`/`truncate`) like a `Math.ceil()`-style operation: a value already exactly on the target field's boundary should be returned unchanged. Instead, `ceiling(28 Mar 2002 13:00:00.000, HOUR_OF_DAY)` returns `14:00:00.000`. In `DateUtils.modify()`, once the loop reaches the matching field it unconditionally does `val.add(fields[i][0], 1)` for `MODIFY_CEILING`, without checking whether the finer-grained fields were already zero (as `MODIFY_ROUND`'s `roundUp` flag correctly does). This makes `ceiling` non-idempotent on exact boundaries, unlike `truncate`/`round`.
